_about: What a forecast trend could mean for people in a fast-growing peri-urban ward like Makarba, read through livelihoods and the right to the city (Lefebvre: the right to live in, use, shape and benefit from the city). Interpretations of a direction of change, written as 'could', never findings. Keys are forecast series ids; 'up'/'down' is chosen by the direction of the forecast. 'who' lists the groups most exposed. Edit freely.

economic.up: Could change who can afford to live, trade and work here.
economic.down: Could squeeze household budgets and informal earnings first.
economic.rightToCity: Economic change decides who can afford to stay and use the city.

development.up: Could change everyday access to services, space and infrastructure.
development.down: Could widen gaps in access to basic services.
development.rightToCity: Who gets the new infrastructure first is a political choice.

social.up: Could reshape health, schooling and care work in households.
social.down: Could add pressure on families and on women's unpaid care work.
social.rightToCity: Social services are part of a fair claim on the city.

political.up: Could change how much residents can be heard and how fairly decisions are made.
political.down: Could make it harder for residents to be heard in decisions about their area.
political.rightToCity: The right to the city includes a voice in shaping it.

city.up: Could make daily life harder for those who spend most time outdoors.
city.down: Could make daily life easier for those who spend most time outdoors.
city.rightToCity: Clean air and liveable streets are shared urban rights.

markets.up: Could signal more investment pressure on land and housing.
markets.down: Could slow investment and construction jobs.
markets.rightToCity: Market pressure on land can push long-time residents out.

NY.GDP.PCAP.CD.up: Rising incomes could bring offices, malls and cafés to the highway, with new jobs for guards, cleaners and delivery riders, but also higher rents nearby.
NY.GDP.PCAP.CD.down: Falling incomes could slow building and household spending, hitting daily-wage work first.
NY.GDP.PCAP.CD.rightToCity: Growth can benefit residents or price them out; who captures the gains matters.

NY.GNP.PCAP.PP.CD.up: More purchasing power could mean more spending at local shops and stalls, if prices do not rise faster.
NY.GNP.PCAP.PP.CD.down: Less purchasing power could push households to cut back and borrow.
NY.GNP.PCAP.PP.CD.rightToCity: Living costs decide whether ordinary families can stay.

NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG.up: Faster growth could pull more commercial projects to the city edge, and more construction work.
NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG.down: Slower growth could delay projects and thin out construction and service jobs.
NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG.rightToCity: Rapid growth often reaches the city edge before services do.

FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG.up: Higher inflation could raise rents, food and transport costs; daily-wage and informal workers feel it first.
FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG.down: Easing prices could relieve household budgets, especially for food and transport.
FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG.rightToCity: When rents outpace wages, the poorest are pushed further out.

SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS.up: More unemployment could push more people into street vending and informal work, raising contests over footpath space.
SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS.down: Falling unemployment could raise commuting and demand for affordable housing near jobs.
SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS.rightToCity: Access to public space for earning a living is a right-to-the-city question.

SL.UEM.1524.ZS.up: More young people without work could need training, public space and safe places to meet.
SL.UEM.1524.ZS.down: More young people in work could raise demand for rentals and transport near job centres.
SL.UEM.1524.ZS.rightToCity: Young people's claim to the city includes jobs and places to gather.

SL.EMP.SELF.ZS.up: More self-employment could mean more carts, stalls and home businesses, and more need for vending zones and licences.
SL.EMP.SELF.ZS.down: Less self-employment could mean more salaried jobs, or the loss of small family businesses.
SL.EMP.SELF.ZS.rightToCity: Informal work depends on access to streets and recognition under vending law.

SL.TLF.CACT.FE.ZS.up: More women in paid work could raise demand for safe transport, street lighting, toilets and childcare.
SL.TLF.CACT.FE.ZS.down: Fewer women in paid work could reduce household income and women's independence.
SL.TLF.CACT.FE.ZS.rightToCity: A city women can move through safely at any hour is part of their right to it.

FS.AST.PRVT.GD.ZS.up: More credit could help small businesses grow, but also fuel land speculation and household debt.
FS.AST.PRVT.GD.ZS.down: Less credit could hold back small businesses that cannot borrow.
FS.AST.PRVT.GD.ZS.rightToCity: Easy credit for developers and hard credit for the poor shapes who owns the city.

NE.CON.PRVT.PC.KD.up: Higher household spending could support local shops, stalls and services.
NE.CON.PRVT.PC.KD.down: Lower spending could hurt the small traders who rely on footfall.

BX.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS.up: More foreign investment could favour big offices and logistics hubs along the highway, often on land once used informally.
BX.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS.down: Less investment could slow large private projects and the jobs they bring.
BX.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS.rightToCity: Big projects can displace informal uses of land without consultation.

NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS.up: More investment could mean more construction: jobs for migrant labourers, but also dust, noise and demolitions.
NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS.down: Less investment could delay roads, drains and housing.
NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS.rightToCity: Who bears the dust and disruption of building, and who gets the result?

NV.IND.MANF.ZS.up: More manufacturing could bring factory jobs and freight traffic to the city edge.
NV.IND.MANF.ZS.down: Less manufacturing could shift work towards services and informal trades, as when Ahmedabad's mills closed.
NV.IND.MANF.ZS.rightToCity: Mill closures in Ahmedabad show how lost industry reshapes whole neighbourhoods.

NV.SRV.TOTL.ZS.up: A growing services sector could mean offices, shops and app-based work such as delivery and ride-hailing.
NV.SRV.TOTL.ZS.down: A shrinking services sector could reduce office and shop jobs.
NV.SRV.TOTL.ZS.rightToCity: Gig workers use the street as their workplace but have few protections there.

BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT.up: More remittances could fund house extensions and small businesses in migrant families.
BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT.down: Fewer remittances could strain families that rely on members working away.
BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT.rightToCity: Migrants build the city but often lack secure claims to it.

SP.POP.TOTL.up: More people overall could crowd water, schools, clinics and buses.
SP.POP.TOTL.down: A slower-growing population could ease pressure on services.
SP.POP.TOTL.rightToCity: Services must keep pace for everyone, not only new developments.

SP.URB.TOTL.IN.ZS.up: Urbanisation could keep turning farmland and village land at the city edge into apartments, changing who lives here and how.
SP.URB.TOTL.IN.ZS.down: Slower urbanisation could ease land pressure at the city edge.
SP.URB.TOTL.IN.ZS.rightToCity: Villages absorbed by the city can lose land, livelihoods and voice.

SP.URB.TOTL.up: More city dwellers could mean more demand for affordable homes, transit and public space.
SP.URB.TOTL.down: Fewer new city dwellers could ease housing pressure.
SP.URB.TOTL.rightToCity: Newcomers need a fair claim to housing and services.

SP.URB.GROW.up: Faster urban growth could outpace drains, roads and schools, as in many peri-urban wards.
SP.URB.GROW.down: Slower urban growth could give infrastructure time to catch up.
SP.URB.GROW.rightToCity: When services lag growth, the poorest wait longest.

EN.POP.DNST.up: Higher density could mean smaller homes and busier streets, but also shops and transit within walking distance.
EN.POP.DNST.down: Lower density could spread the city and lengthen commutes.
EN.POP.DNST.rightToCity: Density can be fair if public space and services grow with it.

EN.URB.MCTY.TL.ZS.up: More people in million-plus cities could deepen Ahmedabad's pull on migrants from across Gujarat and beyond.
EN.URB.MCTY.TL.ZS.down: Slower big-city growth could shift growth to smaller towns.
EN.URB.MCTY.TL.ZS.rightToCity: Big cities attract people faster than they plan for them.

EG.ELC.ACCS.ZS.up: Near-universal electricity could support home businesses, study after dark and phone-based work.
EG.ELC.ACCS.ZS.down: Gaps in electricity would hold back home businesses and students.
EG.ELC.ACCS.ZS.rightToCity: Reliable power is a basic condition of urban life.

EG.ELC.ACCS.UR.ZS.up: Urban electricity coverage closing the last gaps could reach informal settlements, if connections are legal and affordable.
EG.ELC.ACCS.UR.ZS.down: Gaps could remain in informal settlements without legal connections.
EG.ELC.ACCS.UR.ZS.rightToCity: Legal connections are often tied to recognised tenure.

IT.NET.USER.ZS.up: Wider internet use could move jobs, payments and government services online, a gain for many and a barrier for those without phones or skills.
IT.NET.USER.ZS.down: Lower internet use would leave people out of online services.
IT.NET.USER.ZS.rightToCity: As services go digital, digital access becomes part of the right to the city.

IT.CEL.SETS.P2.up: More mobile connections could deepen UPI payments and app-based work for vendors and drivers.
IT.CEL.SETS.P2.down: Fewer connections would narrow digital access.
IT.CEL.SETS.P2.rightToCity: Digital payments can help vendors, if fees and data stay fair.

IT.NET.BBND.P2.up: More broadband could support work from home and online schooling, mostly in better-off homes.
IT.NET.BBND.P2.down: Less broadband would widen the digital divide.

EG.FEC.RNEW.ZS.up: A larger renewable share could bring rooftop solar and EV charging. Owners who control their roofs save money; tenants and informal settlements rarely do. Installation jobs could open up.
EG.FEC.RNEW.ZS.down: A falling renewable share would keep reliance on fossil fuels and polluted air.
EG.FEC.RNEW.ZS.rightToCity: A green transition is fair only if renters and the poor share its benefits.

EG.ELC.RNEW.ZS.up: More renewable electricity could cut air pollution from power, helping everyone, especially outdoor workers.
EG.ELC.RNEW.ZS.down: Less renewable electricity would keep coal's health costs.
EG.ELC.RNEW.ZS.rightToCity: Clean energy is also a public-health and equity question.

EN.ATM.PM25.MC.M3.up: Worse air could hit street vendors, traffic police, auto drivers and children hardest, because they spend the most time outdoors.
EN.ATM.PM25.MC.M3.down: Cleaner air would protect those who live and work beside busy roads.
EN.ATM.PM25.MC.M3.rightToCity: Clean air is unequally shared: the poorest breathe the worst of it.

EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC.up: Higher electricity use could mean more fans, coolers and ACs in a hotter city, with rising bills for poorer homes.
EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC.down: Lower use could ease bills and summer peak loads.
EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC.rightToCity: Staying cool in a heatwave should not depend on income.

EN.GHG.CO2.PC.CE.AR5.up: Rising emissions could add to the heat and floods that hit the poorest settlements first.
EN.GHG.CO2.PC.CE.AR5.down: Falling emissions would ease long-term climate risk.
EN.GHG.CO2.PC.CE.AR5.rightToCity: Climate harm falls first on those who did least to cause it.

EG.ELC.LOSS.ZS.up: More power lost in transmission could mean more outages for households and small businesses.
EG.ELC.LOSS.ZS.down: Fewer losses could mean more reliable power.
EG.ELC.LOSS.ZS.rightToCity: Reliable services are part of a liveable city.

SH.STA.BASS.ZS.up: Better sanitation could improve health and dignity, especially for women and girls.
SH.STA.BASS.ZS.down: Gaps in sanitation would fall hardest on women and informal settlements.
SH.STA.BASS.ZS.rightToCity: Toilets and drains are basic rights in the city.

SH.H2O.BASW.ZS.up: Better water access could free hours women spend collecting water.
SH.H2O.BASW.ZS.down: Gaps in water would mean tanker dependence and higher costs for the poor.
SH.H2O.BASW.ZS.rightToCity: Water access often follows tenure; renters and settlers pay more.

EG.CFT.ACCS.ZS.up: Clean cooking fuel could cut indoor smoke that harms women and children most.
EG.CFT.ACCS.ZS.down: Gaps in clean fuel would keep indoor air pollution high.
EG.CFT.ACCS.ZS.rightToCity: Health at home is shaped by policy on fuel and subsidies.

IS.AIR.PSGR.up: More air travel could signal a growing middle class and business links, with little benefit for most residents.
IS.AIR.PSGR.down: Less air travel would slow business travel.
IS.AIR.PSGR.rightToCity: Investment in elite mobility can crowd out buses and footpaths.

AG.LND.FRST.ZS.up: More tree and forest cover could mean shade and cooler streets, if it reaches dense neighbourhoods.
AG.LND.FRST.ZS.down: Less green cover would make heat worse in dense, poor areas.
AG.LND.FRST.ZS.rightToCity: Shade and green space are unevenly shared across the city.

SP.DYN.LE00.IN.up: Longer lives could raise demand for nearby clinics, step-free streets and benches.
SP.DYN.LE00.IN.down: Falling life expectancy would signal strain on health and living conditions.
SP.DYN.LE00.IN.rightToCity: An ageing city must stay walkable and accessible.

SH.DYN.MORT.up: Rising child mortality would point to gaps in maternal and child health.
SH.DYN.MORT.down: Falling child mortality reflects better care and nutrition.
SH.DYN.MORT.rightToCity: Health care close to home is part of a fair city.

SP.DYN.TFRT.IN.up: Higher fertility could raise future demand for schools and child care.
SP.DYN.TFRT.IN.down: Lower fertility could mean smaller households and, over time, fewer new school places needed.
SP.DYN.TFRT.IN.rightToCity: Household change shapes what homes and services are needed.

SP.POP.65UP.TO.ZS.up: An ageing population would need step-free streets, seating, shade and nearby healthcare, and more care work, mostly done by women.
SP.POP.65UP.TO.ZS.down: A younger population would need more schools and play space.
SP.POP.65UP.TO.ZS.rightToCity: A city built for cars excludes older pedestrians.

SP.POP.0014.TO.ZS.up: More children could need schools, safe routes and play space.
SP.POP.0014.TO.ZS.down: Fewer children could ease school demand over time.
SP.POP.0014.TO.ZS.rightToCity: Children's right to the city includes safe streets to play and walk.

SP.POP.DPND.up: More dependants per worker could stretch household earnings and care time.
SP.POP.DPND.down: Fewer dependants per worker could free income for savings and education.
SP.POP.DPND.rightToCity: Care work keeps the city running but is rarely planned for.

SM.POP.NETM.up: More people moving in could mean more demand for affordable rentals and work, and more pressure on newcomers' rights.
SM.POP.NETM.down: More people leaving could signal lost opportunities.
SM.POP.NETM.rightToCity: Migrants often have the weakest claims to housing and services.

SE.SEC.ENRR.up: More secondary enrolment could raise demand for schools and safe routes to school, especially for girls.
SE.SEC.ENRR.down: Lower enrolment would raise dropout risk.
SE.SEC.ENRR.rightToCity: Safe streets to school matter for girls' education.

SE.TER.ENRR.up: More college enrolment could raise demand for student housing and buses to campuses.
SE.TER.ENRR.down: Lower enrolment would mean fewer students.
SE.TER.ENRR.rightToCity: Affordable student housing affects who can study in the city.

SE.PRM.CMPT.ZS.up: More children completing primary school would widen future opportunities.
SE.PRM.CMPT.ZS.down: Lower completion would point to children leaving school for work.
SE.PRM.CMPT.ZS.rightToCity: Education is a foundation for full urban citizenship.

SE.XPD.TOTL.GD.ZS.up: More education spending could improve public schools that poorer families rely on.
SE.XPD.TOTL.GD.ZS.down: Less spending would push families towards costly private schools.
SE.XPD.TOTL.GD.ZS.rightToCity: Public schools are part of the shared city.

SH.XPD.CHEX.GD.ZS.up: More health spending could support public clinics, reducing out-of-pocket costs.
SH.XPD.CHEX.GD.ZS.down: Less spending would raise costs for families who cannot afford private care.
SH.XPD.CHEX.GD.ZS.rightToCity: Public health care is a common good of the city.

SH.STA.TRAF.P5.up: More road deaths would mean more danger for pedestrians, cyclists and two-wheeler riders.
SH.STA.TRAF.P5.down: Fewer road deaths would mean safer streets for walkers and children.
SH.STA.TRAF.P5.rightToCity: Streets designed for cars put walkers' lives at risk.

SH.STA.SUIC.P5.up: A rising suicide rate would signal distress that needs community and mental-health support.
SH.STA.SUIC.P5.down: A falling rate would suggest improving support and conditions.
SH.STA.SUIC.P5.rightToCity: Social support networks are part of a liveable city.

GB.XPD.RSDV.GD.ZS.up: More research spending could bring knowledge jobs, mostly for the highly educated.
GB.XPD.RSDV.GD.ZS.down: Less research spending would slow innovation.
GB.XPD.RSDV.GD.ZS.rightToCity: Knowledge economies can widen inequality without inclusive training.

NE.EXP.GNFS.ZS.up: More exports could bring factory and logistics jobs to the industrial edge of the city.
NE.EXP.GNFS.ZS.down: Fewer exports could cut factory jobs.

GOV_WGI_PV.EST.up: Greater stability could support long-term investment and everyday security.
GOV_WGI_PV.EST.down: Lower stability could make residents and investors more cautious.
GOV_WGI_PV.EST.rightToCity: Feeling safe in public space is part of the right to the city.

GOV_WGI_GE.EST.up: More effective government could mean faster roads, water connections and permits.
GOV_WGI_GE.EST.down: Less effective government could delay civic works and services.
GOV_WGI_GE.EST.rightToCity: Residents' claims on the city depend on institutions that deliver.

GOV_WGI_RL.EST.up: A stronger rule of law could give clearer land titles and protection from arbitrary eviction.
GOV_WGI_RL.EST.down: A weaker rule of law could make evictions and land disputes more likely.
GOV_WGI_RL.EST.rightToCity: Tenure security is at the heart of the right to stay.

GOV_WGI_CC.EST.up: Better control of corruption could make permits, vending licences and services fairer.
GOV_WGI_CC.EST.down: Weaker control could raise the informal 'cost' vendors and residents pay.
GOV_WGI_CC.EST.rightToCity: Fair, transparent rules protect the weakest users of the city.

GOV_WGI_VA.EST.up: More voice and accountability could strengthen residents' say in planning and ward decisions.
GOV_WGI_VA.EST.down: Less voice could weaken public consultation on projects that affect them.
GOV_WGI_VA.EST.rightToCity: Participation in shaping the city is the core of the right to the city.

GOV_WGI_RQ.EST.up: Better regulation could ease small-business registration and building approvals.
GOV_WGI_RQ.EST.down: Worse regulation could keep small enterprises informal and insecure.
GOV_WGI_RQ.EST.rightToCity: Rules can protect or exclude informal livelihoods.

SG.GEN.PARL.ZS.up: More women in parliament could raise attention to safety, water, care and transport.
SG.GEN.PARL.ZS.down: Fewer women in parliament would narrow whose needs shape policy.
SG.GEN.PARL.ZS.rightToCity: Representation shapes whose city gets planned.

GC.TAX.TOTL.GD.ZS.up: More tax revenue could fund public services and infrastructure.
GC.TAX.TOTL.GD.ZS.down: Less revenue could squeeze public spending on the poorest areas.
GC.TAX.TOTL.GD.ZS.rightToCity: Public finance decides how fairly the city is shared.

KAGGLE_AHD_PM2.5.up: Dirtier air in Ahmedabad could mean more breathing problems for vendors, auto drivers and children beside the highway.
KAGGLE_AHD_PM2.5.down: Cleaner air would most help those who live and work outdoors.
KAGGLE_AHD_PM2.5.rightToCity: The right to breathe clean air is unevenly distributed.

KAGGLE_AHD_NO2.up: More traffic exhaust could strengthen the case for buses, BRTS feeders and EVs.
KAGGLE_AHD_NO2.down: Less exhaust would show cleaner vehicles or more public transport.
KAGGLE_AHD_NO2.rightToCity: Public transport is a more equal use of road space.

KAGGLE_AHD_AQI.up: More bad-air days could keep children and older people indoors and cut outdoor work hours.
KAGGLE_AHD_AQI.down: More clean-air days would make streets usable for everyone.
KAGGLE_AHD_AQI.rightToCity: Unbreathable air takes public space away from everyone.

KAGGLE_AHD_CO.up: More carbon monoxide could come from traffic and burning, worst at junctions.
KAGGLE_AHD_CO.rightToCity: Those who work at junctions breathe the most.

KAGGLE_AHD_SO2.up: More SO₂ could point to industrial and fuel emissions near the factory road.
KAGGLE_AHD_SO2.down: Less SO₂ would mean cleaner industrial air.
KAGGLE_AHD_SO2.rightToCity: Industrial pollution often lands on working-class areas.

KAGGLE_AHD_O3.up: More ground-level ozone could worsen summer breathing problems.
KAGGLE_AHD_O3.down: Less ozone would ease summer air.
KAGGLE_AHD_O3.rightToCity: Heat and smog together hit the most exposed.

WEATHER_AHD_HOTDAYS.up: More days at or above 40 °C could cut outdoor earnings for vendors, construction workers and delivery riders, and endanger older people in homes without cooling.
WEATHER_AHD_HOTDAYS.down: Fewer very hot days would make outdoor work and travel safer.
WEATHER_AHD_HOTDAYS.rightToCity: Shade, water points and cooling centres decide who can safely use the city in summer; Ahmedabad's Heat Action Plan is an example.

WEATHER_AHD_TMAX_SUMMER.up: Hotter summer days could shorten safe working hours outdoors.
WEATHER_AHD_TMAX_SUMMER.down: Cooler summers would ease heat stress.
WEATHER_AHD_TMAX_SUMMER.rightToCity: Heat is a question of who has shade and cooling.

WEATHER_AHD_FEELS_MAX.up: A hotter 'feels like' peak could raise heatstroke risk for people in tin-roofed homes.
WEATHER_AHD_FEELS_MAX.down: A lower peak would reduce heat risk.
WEATHER_AHD_FEELS_MAX.rightToCity: Housing quality decides who suffers in a heatwave.

WEATHER_AHD_RAIN.up: More rain could mean more waterlogging in low-lying lanes and informal settlements.
WEATHER_AHD_RAIN.down: Less rain could stress water supply.
WEATHER_AHD_RAIN.rightToCity: Drainage often reaches richer areas first.

WEATHER_AHD_MONSOON.up: Heavier monsoons could flood roads near the canal and lake and disrupt vendors' trade.
WEATHER_AHD_MONSOON.down: Weaker monsoons could strain water supply and farmers on the city edge.
WEATHER_AHD_MONSOON.rightToCity: Flood risk is unequally shared across the city.

WEATHER_AHD_RAINYDAYS.up: More rainy days could mean more lost workdays for outdoor workers.
WEATHER_AHD_RAINYDAYS.down: Fewer rainy days would mean more outdoor trading days.

WEATHER_AHD_TMIN_WINTER.up: Warmer winter nights would signal a warming climate.
WEATHER_AHD_TMIN_WINTER.down: Colder nights could be hard for people sleeping outdoors.
WEATHER_AHD_TMIN_WINTER.rightToCity: Those without homes are most exposed to weather.

WEATHER_AHD_GUST.up: Stronger gusts could damage stalls, hoardings and tin roofs.
WEATHER_AHD_GUST.down: Calmer weather would reduce storm damage.
WEATHER_AHD_GUST.rightToCity: Storms hit the most fragile structures first.

^NSEI.up: A rising stock market mostly benefits those who own shares, a small share of residents.
^NSEI.down: A falling market could slow investment.
^NSEI.rightToCity: Financial gains rarely reach informal workers.

^CNXREALTY.up: Rising real-estate stocks could signal more land and housing speculation at the city edge, raising rents.
^CNXREALTY.down: Falling real-estate stocks could slow new housing projects.
^CNXREALTY.rightToCity: When land becomes an investment, housing becomes less affordable.

^CNXINFRA.up: Rising infrastructure stocks could mean more roads and flyovers, which can split neighbourhoods as well as connect them.
^CNXINFRA.down: Falling infrastructure stocks could slow projects.
^CNXINFRA.rightToCity: Big infrastructure needs to be planned with the people it passes through.

^NSEBANK.up: Stronger banks could expand credit, mostly to formal borrowers.
^NSEBANK.rightToCity: Access to credit shapes who can own homes and businesses.

INR=X.up: A weaker rupee could raise fuel and import prices, hitting transport costs.
INR=X.down: A stronger rupee could ease import prices.
INR=X.rightToCity: Fuel prices shape who can afford to move around the city.

BZ=F.up: Higher oil prices could raise auto fares and transport costs for everyone.
BZ=F.down: Lower oil prices could ease transport costs.
BZ=F.rightToCity: Mobility costs decide access to jobs.

GC=F.up: Higher gold prices could raise household savings held in gold, a common store of value.
GC=F.down: Lower gold prices could reduce those savings.
GC=F.rightToCity: Household wealth shapes resilience to shocks.
